problem.h2: Copy multiple items – without losing the first one
problem.sub: The Mac clipboard holds exactly one item. Copy two things in a row and the first is lost. Clipsody turns it into a multi-clipboard with a full history.
without: Only the last thing you copied is there.
Back to the other window for every piece of text, copy again, switch again.
Whatever you copied an hour ago is gone.
with: Everything you copied in one list – up to 10,000 clips. You decide how long they stay: from one day to a year.
Copy everything first, then open the list with <kbd>⌥⌘C</kbd> and paste the clips you need, one after the other.
Enter a word, and yesterday’s clip is back.

features.sub: No launcher, no workflows, no hundred settings – a clipboard manager that simply keeps track of what you copy.
cards: One shortcut, everywhere
<kbd>⌥⌘C</kbd> opens your clipboard history in any app. Pick a clip with the arrow keys or enter a search word, press <kbd>⏎</kbd> – the clip lands where you were.
Copy multiple items, paste them when you need them

Copy name, address and order number first, then paste them one by one from the list. <kbd>⌘1</kbd> to <kbd>⌘9</kbd> paste the first nine entries shown directly (of the history or the pinned list, whichever is open).
Finds text in images too
Copied screenshots and images are read on your Mac. Search for a word that appears in the image – and there it is. How it works
Text, images, files
Images are kept lossless, and copied files are pasted as files again – not as a path.
With or without formatting
<kbd>⏎</kbd> keeps bold, links and tables from Word, Outlook or the browser. <kbd>⌥⏎</kbd> pastes plain text only.
Pin what you use often
IBAN, address, snippets, commands: ⌘P moves a clip to its own Pinned list, one → away from the history. How it works

ocr.h2: That screenshot from last week? Just search for the text on it.
ocr.sub: Clipsody reads the text on every image you copy – with macOS text recognition, right on your Mac. So you find screenshots by what they say.
steps: Image on the clipboard
<kbd>⇧⌃⌘4</kbd> captures part of the screen and puts it straight on the clipboard. Or copy an image from any app.
Clipsody reads the text
In the background and on your Mac – nothing is uploaded. English and German text is recognised.
Find it days later
Press <kbd>⌥⌘C</kbd>, enter “0x8007” – there is the screenshot. <kbd>⏎</kbd> pastes it as an image, say into a support ticket.
ocr.note: Good to know: screenshots that macOS only saves as a file on the desktop never reach the clipboard. Add ⌃ to the shortcut for that (⇧⌃⌘3 for the whole screen, ⇧⌃⌘4 for an area).

uses.h2: What a clipboard history is good for
uses.sub: Anywhere you copy more than one thing.
cards: Filling in forms
Collect name, address and order number from an email and paste them into the form one by one – without switching windows ten times.
Writing and research
Copy quotes, links and paragraphs from several sources and put them together later.
Coding
Find commands, paths and snippets you copied hours ago. Pin the commands you use all the time.
Support and office work
Canned replies, account numbers and signatures pinned and ready – pasted in seconds.

privacy.sub: Personal things end up on the clipboard: passwords, addresses, messages. That’s why Clipsody is private by design.
cards: Your clipboard never leaves your Mac
No account, no server, no analytics. The history lives only on your Mac and is excluded from backups. Clipsody only goes online if you allow it – to ask whether there is a new version.
Passwords stay out
Anything password managers mark as concealed is never stored. 1Password, Bitwarden, KeePassXC and others are excluded out of the box.
Deleted means deleted
Deleted entries are overwritten in the database and its change log is emptied – even after a crash, at the next launch. Image files of deleted entries are removed.
Images in a sandbox
Untrusted image data is processed in an isolated helper process without file or network access, not in the app itself.
Verifiable
The source is open. You don’t have to trust anyone – you can read it and build the app yourself.
Kept out of classic screenshots
The window is hidden from screenshots and classic screen sharing. Since macOS 15, modern screen-recording apps can still capture it.

install.sub: Clipsody is not notarised by Apple – that needs a paid developer account. So macOS asks once on first launch – here’s how:
steps: Download Clipsody.dmg, open it and drag Clipsody into Applications.
Launch Clipsody. macOS says it cannot verify the app – click Done. On macOS 13 and 14, right-click Clipsody in Applications → Open → Open instead, and skip step 3.
Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down and choose Open Anyway for Clipsody (macOS 15 and later).
To let ⏎ paste directly, allow Clipsody under Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Without it, the entry is only put on the clipboard and you press ⌘V yourself.
Done: press <kbd>⌥⌘C</kbd>. The menu bar icon leads to the settings, where you can also start Clipsody at login.

items: How do I see what I copied earlier on a Mac?

Out of the box, the Mac only remembers the last thing you copied. A clipboard manager like Clipsody keeps everything you copy: ⌥⌘C shows it all, searchable. Every way, including Finder and the Spotlight history of macOS 26: how to see your clipboard history on a Mac.
How do I copy multiple items and paste them one after another?

With Clipsody you just copy as usual with <kbd>⌘C</kbd> – every clip stays in the history. To paste, open the list with <kbd>⌥⌘C</kbd> and pick a clip with <kbd>⏎</kbd>, or paste one of the first nine directly with <kbd>⌘1</kbd> to <kbd>⌘9</kbd>. A pasted clip moves to the top of the list.
Is Clipsody really free?
Yes. No ads, no subscription, no trial. The source is open, under the GPLv3.
Why does Clipsody need the Accessibility permission?
Only to trigger <kbd>⌘V</kbd> in the app you came from after you pick an entry. Clipsody does not use it to read the screen or your keystrokes. Everything works without it – you just paste yourself.
How long is the history kept?
7 days and at most 1,000 entries by default; you can raise both in the settings, up to 365 days and 10,000 entries. Pinned entries always stay.
Are my passwords stored?

No, if your password manager marks them as concealed – the common ones do. Known password managers are excluded as well. One limit: Clipsody sees which app is in front, not who copied. If a browser extension copies a password without that mark, it ends up in the history – just delete it with <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>.
Does Clipsody run on my Mac?
macOS 13 Ventura or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel.
Which languages does Clipsody speak?
English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish and Brazilian Portuguese. Clipsody follows your Mac’s language; you can pick another one under Settings → General → Language.
Why does macOS ask whether Clipsody may read the clipboard?

Newer versions of macOS ask before an app reads what you copy in other apps. Without this access Clipsody cannot keep a history: choose Allow, or allow Clipsody under System Settings → Privacy & Security. Clipsody shows the current state under Settings → General. Your clipboard still never leaves your Mac.
Does Clipsody check for updates?

Only if you allow it: at the first launch Clipsody asks whether it may ask GitHub once a day for a new version. Nothing from your clipboard is sent; GitHub sees your IP address and the Clipsody version. If there is a new version, the menu bar icon gets a dot, and the menu opens the download page. You can change this under Settings → General; there and in the menu bar menu you can also check yourself at any time.
How do I uninstall Clipsody?

Settings → Info → Uninstall Clipsody… deletes the history, images and settings, removes the login item and the Accessibility permission, and moves the app to the Trash. If you only drag the app to the Trash yourself, this data stays on your Mac.

Email and support
Signatures, answers to common questions, the link to your calendar or the directions to your office.
Invoices and paperwork
IBAN, VAT number, tax ID, reference numbers: no typos, because you copied them only once.
Development and IT
Long commands, server addresses, test data and paths you need every day.
pinned.note: Pinned clips stay: they are never deleted automatically, don’t count towards the history limit and survive clearing the history. Like everything in Clipsody, they stay on your Mac. Passwords still belong in a password manager.

guide.description: How do you see what you copied earlier on a Mac? Finder, the Spotlight clipboard history (macOS 26) and clipboard managers compared, step by step.
guide.ogTitle: How to see clipboard history on a Mac – every way
guide.ogDescription: Finder, the Spotlight clipboard history in macOS 26 and clipboard managers compared, step by step.
guide.h1: How to see your clipboard history on a Mac: every way
guide.lead: You copied something, then something else – and now you need the first one again? Here is what the Mac can do on its own, how the new Spotlight history works, and when a clipboard manager is worth it.
guide.updated: Updated October 2026, macOS 13 Ventura to macOS 27
guide.summary: In short: the Mac clipboard holds only one item; every ⌘C replaces the previous one. Since macOS 26, Spotlight shows recent clips once you turn it on (⌘ Space, then ⌘4). For a lasting, searchable history on any macOS version, use a clipboard manager like Clipsody.

finder.h2: 1. Show the current clipboard in Finder
finder.intro: Finder shows what is on the clipboard right now – but only that one item:
steps: Click the desktop or a Finder window so Finder is in front.
Choose Edit → Show Clipboard in the menu bar.
finder.after: A window shows the content, such as text or an image. Earlier clips are not there: whatever you copied before has been replaced. The clipboard lives in memory, not in a file on disk – after a restart it is empty.

spotlight.h2: 2. The clipboard history in Spotlight (macOS 26 and later)
spotlight.intro: With macOS 26 Tahoe, Apple gave Spotlight a clipboard history. It is off by default.
steps: Open Spotlight with <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd>.
Press <kbd>⌘4</kbd>, or click the clipboard button to the right of the search field.
The first time, macOS asks whether to turn the history on – confirm.
Find the clip, copy it with the copy button or <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, and paste it with <kbd>⌘V</kbd> where you need it.
spotlight.after: Good for the moment, with limits: depending on the setting, clips are kept for 30 minutes, 8 hours or 7 days; there is no pinning, and pasting takes two steps (copy, then <kbd>⌘V</kbd>). Macs on macOS 15 or earlier don’t have it. You can clear it from the menu to the right of the search field.

manager.h2: 3. Every clip with a clipboard manager
manager.intro: A clipboard manager (also called a clipboard history app or multi-clipboard) remembers everything you copy and brings it back on demand. Here is how it works with Clipsody, the free clipboard manager for Mac (macOS 13 and later):
steps: Download Clipsody and drag it into Applications (installation in detail).
Copy as usual with <kbd>⌘C</kbd>. Every clip – text, image or file – goes into the history.
Press <kbd>⌥⌘C</kbd>: the list of everything you copied appears. Enter a search word to filter it; this finds text in screenshots too.

<kbd>⏎</kbd> pastes the selected clip right where you were; <kbd>⌥⏎</kbd> pastes it without formatting. <kbd>⌘1</kbd> to <kbd>⌘9</kbd> paste the first nine entries shown directly (of the history or the pinned list, whichever is open).
manager.after: You decide how long the history lasts (1 to 365 days) and how many clips it holds (up to 10,000). Clips pinned with <kbd>⌘P</kbd> stay for good. Everything stays on your Mac.

rows: Paste without formatting (“Paste and Match Style”, in many apps)
Screenshot of an area straight to the clipboard

items: Where is the clipboard stored on a Mac?
In memory, not in a file. That’s why it is empty after a restart, and there is no folder holding earlier clips. A saved history only exists with Spotlight (macOS 26 and later) or a clipboard manager.
Can I get back what was on the clipboard before I copied something else?
Only if a history was recording: the Spotlight history on macOS 26 and later, if turned on, or a clipboard manager like Clipsody. Without one, the previous clip is replaced by the next copy.
Can I copy multiple things at once?

The clipboard itself holds a single item. With a clipboard manager you simply copy one thing after another – each clip is kept – and then paste the ones you need. In Clipsody, for example, with <kbd>⌘1</kbd> to <kbd>⌘9</kbd>.
How do I clear the clipboard on a Mac?

Copy something harmless, such as a space – it replaces the current content. Clear the Spotlight history from the menu to the right of its search field, and Clipsody’s history from the menu bar icon → Clear History….
Do iPhone and Mac share a clipboard?

Yes, with Universal Clipboard: with the same Apple Account and Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and Handoff turned on, you can copy on your iPhone and paste on your Mac. It also transfers only the current clip, not a history.
